These two clauses mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could combine them and express the emphasis in another way. Alternate translation: [And I will surely establish them and not destroy them]

Yahweh is speaking as if the people of Judah were a building that he would **build** up and not **tear** down. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And I will cause them to prosper and not ruin them]

This is a double negative, consisting of the negative particle **not** and the negative words **tear them down** and **uproot them**. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a positive expression to translate this. Alternate translation: [and keep them safe, and I will plant them and let them remain there]

Yahweh is speaking as if the people of Judah were a tree that he would **plant** and not **uproot**. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I will establish them permanently and not drive them away]

The pronoun **them** refers to the people of Judah whom Yahweh sent away into exile. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and I, I will be to those exiles from Judah for God]

The word translated as **for** indicates that what follows is a reason for what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that what follows is a reason for what came before. Alternate translation: [because they will return to me with all of their heart]
